messages.author: a81b83f626ae560a
messages.subject: Actigraph .csv / .CSV read in problem
parts:
Dear Vincent 

I have trouble to import Actigraph (from ActigraphCorp) .CSW files into GGIR.

Curiously, I have also seen different kinds of csv files based on the data retrievalchosen.

If I download data as gt3x file from the ActigraphCorp CentrePoint Website and then export it to csv in actilife, I get a lower case .csv file with this file header (opened in Notepad, different study but same type of actigraphs, since I don't have access to ActiLife Software atm):

------------ Data File Created By ActiGraph GT3X+ ActiLife v6.13.4 Firmware v1.2.0 date format dd.MM.yyyy at 30 Hz  Filter Normal -----------,, Serial Number: CPW1B51180317,, Start Time 00:00:00,, Start Date 27.11.2019,, Epoch Period (hh:mm:ss) 00:00:00,, Download Time 11:40:10,, Download Date 09.01.2020,, Current Memory Address: 0,,

Current Battery Voltage: 4.19     Mode = 12,,

--------------------------------------------------,,

Accelerometer X,Accelerometer Y,Accelerometer Z

-0.785,0.625,0.355

-0.715,0.582,0.32

-0.738,0.598,0.344

 

On the other hand, if I download the data directly as .CSV raw data from CentrePoint, the file header looks like this:

#-----Data File Created By CP3 Data Retrieval------ #Serial Number: CPW1B17190046 #Start Date: 2020-03-09 15:21:00 UTC #Download Date: 2020-05-17 07:19:31 UTC #Sample Rate: 32

#--------------------------------------------------

Timestamp UTC,Accelerometer X,Accelerometer Y,Accelerometer Z

2020-03-10 15:21:00,0.54276184168604,-0.38168359810515,0.81464780632169

2020-03-10 15:21:00,0.60093267025978,-0.41479302253295,0.90063158943769


The first kind can be read into GGIR without problem. The second kind ist not read in with this error message:

Error in if (dformat == 1 & is.mv == FALSE) { :
argument is of length zero

If I then change the suffix manually, I get this:

Error in data.frame(value = H[RowsWithData, 2], row.names = H[RowsWithData, : duplicate row.names:
I've tried several things to see the effect, including removing the hashtags (same error as above)  or trying to specify the parameters with rmc arguments:

When I use this arguments in read.myacc.csv

myacc <- read.myacc.csv(rmc.file='C:/Users/testuser/ggir_test/commas_added.csv',
               rmc.firstrow.acc = 8,
               rmc.firstrow.header = 1,
               rmc.header.length = 7,
               rmc.col.acc = c(2, 3, 4),
               rmc.col.time = 1,
               rmc.headername.sn = "2",
               rmc.header.structure = ": "
)

Then I can read in the data, but not the header.

When I transfer the arguments to the GGIR function:

library(GGIR)
GGIR(
  #=====================
  # General parameters
  #=====================
  # rmc.firstrow.header = 1,
  # rmc.header.length = 7,
  # rmc.headername.sn = "2",
  # rmc.headername.sf = "5",
  # rmc.header.structure = ": ",
  #
  #
  # rmc.firstrow.acc = 8,
  # rmc.col.acc = c(2, 3, 4),
  # rmc.col.time = 1,

This gives me this error message:
1 Error in if (Pusercsvformat$header != "no header") { : argument is of length zero

When I remove the header altogether it stops like this:

Part 1 Checking that user has read access permission for all files in data directory: Yes Checking that user has write access permission for directory specified by argument outputdir: Yes 1 P1 file 1 Investigate calibration of the sensors with function g.calibrate: Loading chunk: 1Error in as.POSIXlt.character(P[, 1], tz = params_general[["desiredtz"]]) : character string is not in a standard unambiguous format


I'm a bit at a loss. Do you or someone else in the mailing list have an idea how to solve this issue?

Best regards!
Christian

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Actigraph .csv / .CSV read in problem
parts:
Hi Christian,

Reading in csv is not going to work as ActiGraph seems to have changed their csv file format for this new service and GGIR only knows how to deal with one ActiGraph csv file format.

If gt3x file is not available the best next option is then to use GGIR's functionality to read ad-hoc csv file formats as you did: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/readmyacccsv.html
The header you are trying to read does not meet the header criteria, so you will need to skip those arguments for header extraction.

See here our unit-test that demonstrate how it can handle headers:https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/tests/testthat/test_read.myacc.csv.R

I think with the following 
you are nearly there:

GGIR(rmc.firstrow.acc = 8,

the main thing that seems to be going wrong in your last error is the timestamp recognition.

Can you try to go back to  read.myacc.csv() and explore the specification of the timestamp format and timezone until that function produces a clear POSIX class column. Note that this functionality has improved in the recent 2.9-0 release, so maybe update GGIR is part of the trick.

Best regards,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
